title: Stack
short: Last in, first out. You only touch the top.
what: A stack is a pile. You add to the top (push) and take from the top (pop), so the last thing in is the first thing out. In Python a plain list is a stack: append pushes, pop pops.
analogy: A stack of plates. You put clean plates on top and take the top one. Nobody pulls a plate from the bottom.

frames.say: Task: are the brackets in "([]{})" matched? Read left to right with an empty stack.
Read '('. An opener has to wait for its closer, so push it.
Read '['. Push it on top. The top is always the bracket that must close first.
Read ']'. The top is '[', its partner. Pop it off.
'(' is on top again. Read '{' and push it.
Read '}': the top '{' matches, pop. Then read ')': now '(' is on top, and it matches too.
The input is done and the stack is empty, so every bracket closed in the right order. A wrong top or a leftover means invalid.

when: Walk a tree or graph without recursion
watch: Popping or reading stack[-1] on an empty stack raises IndexError. Check if stack first.
Push and pop at the end of the list. pop(0) is slow and makes it a queue.
At the end, leftover items often mean the answer is no.
